% -----------------------
\subsection{Jershon} % *JERSHON
% -----------------------

	A place on the BOM, where the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi receive an inheritance.
	
	First paragraph from the onomasticon (I have removed some of the letters with diacritical marks, so have not reproduced this exactly):
		JERSHON is probably from the HEBREW root yrš, ``to inherit'' (JWW), in the nominal form *yirs (this qitl form as a possible HEBREW Vorlage has been suggested by SDR) and with ending -on[1], yielding the GN yerson, ``place of inheritance'' (JAT, JH, and more recently, Ricks/Tvedtnes with ample commentary and notes). The HEBREW word yeresa ``inheritance'' (Numbers 24:18), appears to be a feminine noun close to Book of Mormon JERSHON (JAT). Compare also the biblical feminine PNs yerusa' and yerusa (Jerusha/Jerushah, ``Inherited One, Inheritance'' in the KJV;[2] see 2 Kings 15:33 and 2 Chronicles 27:1), and yerussa ``inheritance, possession'' = Samaritan Pentateuch yarišša (Deuteronomy 2:5,9,12,19, Joshua 1:15, Jeremiah 32:8).[3] The same root probably stands behind the Ugaritic PNs yrt, ``Heir,'' and iarisunu (JH). The same root stands behind Old South Arabic wrt, Arabic warita ``inherit,'' and probably Akkadian rasu ``take possession of.''

\subsection{Joseph Smith} % *JOSEPHSMITH
% -----------------------

	\begin{description}
	\item[CDBY 25] Who called Joseph Smith to be a prophet? Did the people or God? God, and not the people called him. Had the people gathered together and appointed one of their number to be a prophet, he would have been accountable to the people; but inasmuch as he was called by God, and not the people, he is accountable to God only and the angel who committed the gospel to him, and not to any man on earth.
	\item[CDBY 26] Who is the author of this work and gathering? Joseph Smith, the Prophet, as an instrument in the hands of God, is the author of it. He is the greatest man on earth. No other man, at this age of the world, has power to assemble such a great people from all the nations of the earth, with all their varied dispositions, and so assimilate and cement them together that they become subject to rule and order. This the Prophet Joseph is doing. He has already gathered a great people who willingly subject themselves to his counsel, because they know it is righteous.
	\item[CDBY 37] Joseph said he was not known in our midst. He might live and die and not be fully known until he was weighed in the balance in the eternal world.
	\item[CDBY 38] Spent the day in Boston with brother Woodruff, who accompanied me to the railway station as I was about to take cars to Salem. In the evening, while sitting in the depot waiting, I felt a heavy depression of spirit, and so melancholy I could not converse with any degree of pleasure. Not knowing anything concerning the tragedy enacting at this time in Carthage Jail [Joseph's death], I could not assign my reasons for my peculiar feeling.
	\item[CDBY 38] When God sends a man to do a work, all the devils in hell cannot kill him until he gets through his work; so with Joseph, he prepared all things, gave the keys to men on the earth, and said, ``I may soon be taken from you.''
	\item[CDBY 39] Joseph conferred upon our heads all the keys and powers belonging to the Apostleship which he himself held before he was taken away, and no man or set of men can get between Joseph and the Twelve in this world or in the world to come. How often has Joseph said to the Twelve, `I have laid the foundation and you must build thereon, for upon your shoulders the kingdom rests.'
	\item[CDBY 44] You did not know who you had amongst you. Joseph so loved this people that he gave his life for them; Hyrum loved his brother and this people unto death. Joseph and Hyrum have given their lives for the church. But very few knew Joseph's character; he loved you unto death----you did not know it until after his death: he has now sealed his testimony with his blood. If the Twelve had been here we would not have seen him given up---he should not have been given up. He was in your midst, but you did not know him; he has been taken away, for the people are not worthy of him.
	\item[CDBY 44] There is much to be done. You have men among you who sleep with one eye open. The foundation is laid by our Prophet, and we will build thereon; no other foundation can be laid but that which is laid, and we will have our endowment, if the Lord will.
	\item[CDBY 44] We can build on the foundation that was laid by the Prophet. Joseph has finished his work, and all the devils in hell and all the mobbers on earth could not take his life until he had accomplished his work. God said, I will put a veil over his eyes and lead him up to the slaughter like a sheep to be killed, for the people are not worthy of him, though God loves this people.
	\item[CDBY 45] When the solemn event took place, the Twelve Apostles were nearly all absent. They soon returned, and we were all anxiety to know what they would say. President Brigham Young spoke words which pierced my heart like a dagger! Said he, ``Had I been here, Joseph should not have gone to Carthage!''
	\item[CDBY 54] Are the keys of the kingdom taken from Joseph? Oh no; well then he still lives. He that believes in Jesus as Joseph did, they will never die They may lay down their lives, but they still hold the keys.
	\item[CDBY 54--55] When did Joseph become a Prophet? I can tell you, when he became an Apostle. Years and years before he had the right of holding the keys of the Aaronic priesthood, he was a Prophet, even before he was baptized.
	\item[Brigham Young, JD 8:15--16] I recollect that while on my way to Ohio, to see brother Joseph the first time, I took dinner with a Mr. Gillmore---I think a Methodist priest. He began to tell me the character of Joseph Smith, what he had been guilty of, how long he had been a money-digger, how long a horse-jockey, and how many horses he had stolen; and his statement made Joseph to be some seventy or eighty years of age. I said to him, "Joseph Smith I never saw. He says that he has received revelations from God, and declared that an angel visited him. He has declared that he found plates, and other witnesses have seen and handled them, from which the Book of Mormon was translated. I know nothing about these witnesses, neither do I care. I went to my Father in heaven and asked him with regard to the truth of the doctrines taught by Joseph Smith, and I know they will save all that will hearken to them, and that those who do not will miss salvation in the celestial kingdom of God; and though Joseph Smith should steal horses every day, or gamble every night, or deny his Saviour from the crowing of the cock in the morning until sunset in the evening, I know that the doctrine he preaches is the power of God to my salvation, if I live it. I did not make him a revelator; I have no business to dictate him. I never called him in question, even in my feelings, for an act of his, except once. I did not like his policy in a matter, and a feeling came into my heart that would have led me to complain; but it was much shorter lived than Jonah's gourd, for it did not last half a minute.
	\end{description}

Then again we say: Search the Scriptures, search the Prophets and learn what portion of them belongs to you and the people of the nineteenth century.
		\item[TPJS 12--13] Wherefore, we again say, search the revelations of God; study the prophecies, and rejoice that God grants unto the world Seers and Prophets. They are they who saw the mysteries of godliness; they saw the flood before it came; they saw angels ascending and descending upon a ladder that reached from earth to heaven; they saw the stone cut out of the mountain, which filled the whole earth; they saw the Son of God come from the regions of bliss and dwell with men on earth; they saw the deliverer come out of Zion, and turn away ungodliness from Jacob; they saw the glory of the Lord when he showed the transfiguration of the earth on the mount; they saw every mountain laid low and every valley exalted when the Lord was taking vengeance upon the wicked; they saw truth spring out of the earth, and righteousness look down from heaven in the last days, before the Lord came the second time to gather his elect; they saw the end of wickedness on earth, and the Sabbath of creation crowned with peace; they saw the end of the glorious thousand years, when Satan was loosed for a little season; they saw the day of judgment when all men received according to their works, and they saw the heaven and the earth flee away to make room for the city of God, when the righteous receive an inheritance in eternity. And, fellow sojourners upon earth, it is your privilege to purify yourselves and come up to the same glory, and see for yourselves, and know for yourselves. Ask, and it shall be given you; seek and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
		\item[TPJS 22] There are two paragraphs in your letter which I do not commend, as they are written blindly. Speaking of the Elders being sent like lightning from the bow of Judah; the second, no secret in the councils of Zion. You mention these as if fear rested upon your mind, otherwise we cannot understand it. And again we never inquire at the hand of God for special revelation only in case of there being no previous revelation to suit the case; and that in a council of High Priests...It is a great thing to inquire at the hands of God, or to come into His presence; and we feel fearful to approach Him on subjects that are of little or no consequence, to satisfy the queries of individuals, especially about things the knowledge of which men ought to obtain in all sincerity, before God, for themselves, in humility by the prayer of faith
		\end{description}

	% -----
	\subsubsection{Stories similar to JS}
	% -----
	
		\begin{compactdesc}
		\item[2 Baruch] (This is the text of an email sent to me by Erik Yingling.) There is a tale in 2 Baruch about the destruction of the Jews during the time of Lehi that is quite similar to the BOM destruction and burial of plates. 

		In the prophecy an angel comes down from heaven and commands the earth to receive the tablets of the law, the ark (i.e. a box), the priest's stones and other temple relics. The angel cries out to the earth:

		(2 Baruch 6:3--10.) ``And lo! suddenly a strong spirit raised me, and bore me aloft over the wall of Jerusalem. 4 And I beheld, and lo! four angels standing at the four corners of the city, each of them holding a torch of fire in his hands. 5 And another angel began to descend from heaven. and said unto them: 'Hold your lamps, and do not light them till I tell you. 6 For I am first sent to speak a word to the earth, and to place in it what the Lord the Most High has commanded me.' 7 And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from there the veil, and holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle. 8 And he spoke to the earth with a loud voice: `Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the mighty God, And receive what I commit to you, And guard them until the last times, So that, when you are ordered, you may restore them, So that strangers may not get possession of them. 9 For the time comes when Jerusalem also will be delivered for a time, Until it is said, that it is again restored for ever.' 10 And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up.''

		The correspondences are so strong with the BOM: angels, the destruction of a people, the holy tablets and sacred relics placed in the earth, awaiting a time of restoration. Perhaps the Nephites knew of these sorts of traditions and this provided the impetus and faith needed to bury the plates, the stones, etc.

		Although this text is dated to the destruction in 70 (rather than 600 BC) it makes me wonder if the tradition echoes a much earlier cultural memory. After all it is said that the ark disappeared after the first destruction.
		\end{compactdesc}
		
	% -----
	\subsubsection{Joseph Smith as Holy Ghost}
	% -----
	
		\begin{description}
		\item[Vern G. Swanson, ``The Development of the Concept of a Holy Ghost in Mormon Theology,'' in \textit{Line Upon Line: Essays on Mormon Doctrine}] There are other theories regarding the identity of the Holy Ghost attributed to Joseph Smith. The most widespread is the belief that Smith was the Holy Ghost; or more correctly stated, that he represented the emanating spirit of the Father and the Son. This theory arose from several sources. In a 9 March 1841 discourse Joseph Smith apparently discussed three gods who covenanted to preside over this creation: ``[An] Everlasting Covenant was made between three personages before the organization of this earth, and [it] relates to their dispensation of things to men on the earth.'' These three gods, some argue, were Father Adam for the beginning of the mortal world, Christ for the Meridian of Time, and Joseph Smith for the Dispensation of the Fullness of Times. Others have seen Doctrine and Covenants 135:3 as evidence for Smith being the Holy Ghost: ``Joseph Smith, the Prophet and Seer of the Lord, has done more, save Jesus only, for the salvation of men in this world than any other man that ever lived in it.'' Accordingly, Christ did the most to save humanity and is the second member of the Godhead; therefore, Smith, who did second to the most, is the third member.

		That such notions have circulated in the church since 1844 is made clear by comments from church leaders contradicting these views. In August 1845 Orson Pratt wrote to church members responding to rumors that Joseph Smith was the Holy Ghost incarnate: ``Let no false doctrine proceed out of your mouth, such, for instance that the tabernacle of our martyred prophet and seer, or of any other person, was or is the especial tabernacle of the Holy Ghost, in a different sense from that considered in relation to his residence in other tabernacles. These are doctrines not revealed, and are neither believed nor sanctioned by the Twelve and should be rejected by every Saint.''

		Similarly, in January 1845, Brigham Young responded to conjectures about what Joseph Smith may have meant when Smith said, ``Would to God, brethren I could tell you who I am! Would to God I could tell you what I know! But you would call it blasphemy and want to take my life.'' Young specifically countered any interpretation that Smith was the Holy Ghost: ``[Y]ou have heard Joseph say that the people did not know him; he had his eyes on the relation to blood-relations. Some have supposed that he meant spirit [Holy Ghost], but it was the blood-relation. This is it that he referred to. His descent from Joseph that was sold into Egypt was direct and the blood was pure in him'' (See CDBY 64).
		
		\item[BY, March 9 1845, Nauvoo High Priests Quorum Record, PDF 97] He said There are many elders in this church that never can hold the keys of this kingdom until their blood becomes changed---and they become of the right seed---Joseph told you you did not know who he was---some thought he was the Holy Ghost---and actually taught it---but I will tell you what he meant---He had reference to the blood---and that is enough for you to know at present.
		\end{description}

% -----------------------
\subsection{Journal History} % *JOURNALHISTORY
% -----------------------

	A source for church history. From the Church History Library website:
		``The Journal History did not actually begin in 1830. It was started in 1906 by Andrew Jenson, the Assistant Church Historian. He used information from previous Church Historians to retroactively compile this documentary history. In the 25 years prior to 1906, Jenson had gathered a variety of sources to publish histories and biographies, including his Church Chronology. He used the sources gathered for these projects to create the Journal History, and its organization undoubtedly arose from Jenson's interest in chronology. Some of the early sources used were Joseph Smith's histories, Brigham Young's manuscript history, the Deseret News, and the Church Historian's Office Journal.
		``By 1913, Jenson had completed the years 1830–1852. By 1918 he was up to 1872, and at his death in 1941, the Journal History had reached the year 1930. His work was continued by staff working for the Church Historian's Office (now known as the Church History Department). In 2008 an administrative decision was made to cease compilation of the Journal History.''

\subsection{Justice} % *JUSTICE
% -----------------------

	\begin{description}
	\item[2N 9:46] Prepare your souls for that glorious day when justice shall be administered unto the righteous, even the day of judgment, that ye may not shrink with awful fear; that ye may not remember your awful guilt in perfectness, and be constrained to exclaim: Holy, holy are thy judgments, O Lord God Almighty---but I know my guilt; I transgressed thy law, and my transgressions are mine; and the devil hath obtained me, that I am a prey to his awful misery.

	\item[3N 28:34--35] And wo be unto him that will not hearken unto the words of Jesus, and also to them whom he hath chosen and sent among them; for whoso receiveth not the words of Jesus and the words of those whom he hath sent receiveth not him; and therefore he will not receive them at the last day; 35 And it would be better for them if they had not been born. For do ye suppose that ye can get rid of the justice of an offended God, who hath been trampled under feet of men, that thereby salvation might come?
	\end{description}

	% -----
	\subsubsection{Where does it come from?}
	% -----
	
		I think the idea of ``demands of justice'' is important here.

		\begin{description}
		\item[2N 9:25--26] Wherefore, he has given a law; and where there is no law given there is no punishment; and where there is no punishment there is no condemnation; and where there is no condemnation the mercies of the Holy One of Israel have claim upon them, because of the atonement; for they are delivered by the power of him. 26 For the atonement satisfieth the demands of his justice upon all those who have not the law given to them, that they are delivered from that awful monster, death and hell, and the devil, and the lake of fire and brimstone, which is endless torment; and they are restored to that God who gave them breath, which is the Holy One of Israel.
		\item[Mo 15:27] Therefore ought ye not to tremble? For salvation cometh to none such; for the Lord hath redeemed none such; yea, neither can the Lord redeem such; for he cannot deny himself; for he cannot deny justice when it has its claim.
		\end{description}

		Here are some scriptures about justice, along with what they say about it:
		Mosiah 15:27: Justice as an (innate?) property of God; God can't deny himself/justice; justice has claim
		2N 9:26: Demands of justice; justice as a property --``his justice'' (God's)
		Al 34:16: Demands of justice; ``the law of the demands of justice''
		1N 12:18: ``Word of the justice of the Eternal God''; justice as a property of God
		Al 42:14

		In Alma 42, it is mentioned several times that God could cease to be God. Here are the circumstances.

		God could cease to be God if...

			the work of justice were destroyed (13),
			
			the works of justice were destroyed (22/23),
			
			mercy robbed justice, even ``one whit'' (25; a ``whit'' means ``a very small part or amount.'' So here, if mercy robbed justice at all).
			
			(Note that Morm 9:19 says that God would cease to be God if he changed.)
			
		In each of the three circumstances (explicitly in the third), mercy would destroy the work of justice by ``claiming'' or saving someone that had not repented. So the particular ``work'' of justice here seems to be ``executing'' the law (22) and inflicting a punishment (22). The law must be executed, and punishment must come. In my mind I have lately been inclined to take a ``naturalized'' view of the harmfulness of sin, wherein sin's harmfulness consists in our loss of opportunities to become more like Jesus Christ (time, circumstances, relationships with others, etc.). While I think that loss of opportunity is one of the harmful effects of sin, I don't think it can be the only one, judging by these verses. A real, retributive punishment must come, something that goes beyond the loss of opportunity, I think; but what is that punishment? I might be able to analyze it in terms of opportunity lost but right now I'm thinking it is something separate.

Why? Because Joseph was their file leader, and he has committed into their hands the keys of the kingdom in this last dispensation, for all the world; don't put a thread between the priesthood and God.
	\item[CDBY 42] I will ask, who has stood next to Joseph and Hyrum? I have, and I will stand next to him. We have a head, and that head is the Apostleship, the spirit and power of Joseph, and we can now begin to see the necessity of that Aposdeship. Brother Rigdon was at his side---not above. No man has a right to counsel the Twelve but Joseph Smith. Think of these things. You cannot appoint a prophet; but if you let the Twelve remain and act in their place, the keys of the kingdom are with them and they can manage the affairs of the church and direct all things aright.
	\item[CDBY 50--51] On Tuesday last, I heard that elder Rigdon had a meeting the night previous, and had ordained men to be prophets, priests and kings. I concluded to go and see elder Rigdon, and asked elder Hyde to go with me. We went into his house, and after the usual compliments, I set down directly opposite him, and took hold of his hand. I looked him right in the face and asked him if he had a meeting last night, here, in which men were ordained to be prophets, priests and kings? He replied no, we had no meeting here; had we Brother Soby? ``Well, did you have a meeting anywhere, brother Rigdon, in which men were ordained to be prophets, priests and kings?'' ``Well, I don't know; did we have a meeting last night, Brother Soby? Yes, I believe there was one last night; wasn't there Brother Soby, up at your house?'' I saw the disposition of elder Rigdon to conceal the truth and equivocate, and I determined to know the whole secret. I said to him again, ``Elder Rigdon, did you not ordain those men at that meeting last night?'' He replied, ``yes, I suppose I did.'' I then asked brother Rigdon, by what authority he ordained prophets, priests and kings? With a very significant air he replied ``oh, I know all about that!'' I will not attempt to describe the feelings I had, nor the look of his countenance, but he equivocated very much. He said there was no meeting here last night, and then finally said, I believe there was a meeting at Brother Soby's. I questioned him till he acknowledged that they ordained men to be prophets, priests and kings. I then asked brother Rigdon; ``do you not think, really, that you hold keys and authority above any man, or set of men in this church, even the Twelve?'' Says he, ``I never taught any such doctrine, did I, Brother Soby?'' Says I, ``brother Rigdon, tell me the truth, do you not think so?'' He replied, ``yes I do.'' Says I, ``that tells the whole story. Brother Joseph never undertook such important business as you are engaged in, without consulting his brethren, and especially the Twelve, if they were present.'' I felt delicate in asking elder Rigdon these questions, but I knew it was my duty to find out the secret of the whole matter. To evade answering the questions put to him, he finally said don't crowd upon my feelings too much; my feelings are tender, and I don't wish to be crowded. I then proposed to him, that myself and the brethren of the Twelve would call in the evening and converse with him further on the subject, to which he agreed. In the evening eight of the Twelve together with bishop Whitney, went to elder Rigdon's and conversed a while; and finding matters as before stated, we concluded we would go over to Dr. Richards' and there council together what was best to do on the subject. In our council we deemed it necessary to demand his license, and say to him he could not hold it any longer, unless he retracted from his present course and repent of his wickedness. A committee of three was chosen, who went over and demanded his license, but he refused to give it up, at the same time saying, ``I did not receive it from you, neither shall I give it up to you.'' On the strength of this, we published a notice in the Neighbor that there would be an action on his case before the church to-day.

		\begin{description}
		\item[1N 15:26--29, 35 \& Hel 3:29--30] As Nephi explains Lehi's vision, he mentions that the river is a gulf separating the righteous from the wicked, and later he clarifies (in 35) that the river is hell after judgment. But Hel 3:29--30 says that this gulf can be crossed by the ``man of Christ.''
		\item[2N 9:16, 19 \& DC 19:12] 2N 9:19 says that God saves the saints from ``the lake of fire and brimstone, which is endless torment.'' From verse 16 it is clear that this lake and torment come \textit{after} the resurrection and the judgment. But DC 19:12 says that ``endless punishment''---which I'm taking to be similar enough to ``endless torment''---is really God's punishment, not necessarily endless. So if it isn't endless, it has an end, and if it has an end then there may be an opportunity for those who are experiencing it to move on to something better and progress.

% -----------------------
\subsection{Knowledge in the scriptures} % *KNOWLEDGEINTHESCRIPTURES *KNOWLEDGESCRIPTURES
% -----------------------

	See Eth 3:19--20; ``he had faith no longer, for he knew, nothing doubting.'' See knowledge as not doubting---this might be a small support for the idea that the knowledge that counts for us (when it comes to accountability) isn't what's true, but what we sincerely believe (in this case, what we don't doubt). This makes some room for a concept of knowledge in the gospel that leaves out truth. And remember DC 93:24, ``truth is knowledge of things as they are...'' So falsity would be knowledge of things as they aren't, maybe? It would be a weaker sense of knowledge, one that doesn't require truth, but that allows us to think about accountability in a fairer way, because it's dependent on what people sincerely believe?

		\item[OJBYD 31] Pres. Young observed to W. C. Staines he had read an article of this weeks `\textit{Valley Tan}' Jan. 25, 1860, which branded the whole Mormon Hierarchy as murderers, and observed the Pres., ``I wonder how the brethren submit to be tamely insulted by the Editor of the \textit{Tan}, M$^{r}$ De Wolf.'' 		\item[Thomas Monson, October 2015 GC] The words we use can lift and inspire, or they can harm and demean. In the world today there is a profusion of profanity with which we seem to be surrounded at nearly every turn. It is difficult to avoid hearing the names of Deity being used casually and thoughtlessly. Coarse comments seem to have become a staple of television, movies, books, and music. Bandied about are slanderous remarks and angry rhetoric. Let us speak to others with love and respect, ever keeping our language clean and avoiding words or comments that would wound or offend. May we follow the example of the Savior, who spoke with tolerance and kindness throughout His ministry.

\subsection{Last Days} % *LASTDAYS
% -----------------------
% ----------------------

	Peter thinks that they are in the last days when he quotes Joel in Acts 2:14--21. JS and others thought that the last days were when they were alive. I don't see a good reason to think that these are the last days now.
		
% -----------------------
\subsection{Law} % *LAWS
% -----------------------

	A ``law'' as spoken of in 2N 2 and 2N 9, for example, seems to be a statement about consequences for action: ``if you do A, then B will happen; but if you do C, then D will happen.'' This way of thinking about a law binds it up with the idea of a consequence, and so the scriptures often mention punishment in connection with a law like this.
		See Locke's \textit{Essay}, part II, chapter 28, section 6.
			Compare this to blessings and laws in DC 130; can the naturalistic view of blessings work?
	
	But something like the ``law of Christ'' in DC 88 seems to go beyond that; it seems more like the physical laws of science, giving structure to the way things exist, as when you read DC 88:21 and then 13.
	
	Note ``law'' in DC 128:9, which is more about something binding in heaven, or something like that.

	\begin{description}
	\item[2N 2] A number of scriptures.

		\item[7] Behold, he offereth himself a sacrifice for sin, to answer the ends of the law, unto all those who have a broken heart and a contrite spirit; and unto none else can the ends of the law be answered.

	\item[DC 132:12] I am the Lord thy God; and I give unto you this commandment---that no man shall come unto the Father but by me or by my word, which is my law, saith the Lord.
	\item[Ps 19:7] The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.
	\item[Pro 6:23] For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
	\item[TPJS 49--50] All regularly organized and well established governments have certain laws by which, more or less, the innocent are protected and the guilty punished. The fact admitted that certain laws are good, equitable and just, ought to be binding upon the individual who admits this, and lead him to observe in the strictest manner an obedience to those laws. These laws when violated, or broken by the individual, must, in justice, convict his mind with a double force, if possible, of the extent and magnitude of his crime; because he could have no plea of ignorance to produce; and his act of transgression was openly committed against light and knowledge. But the individual who may be ignorant and imperceptibly transgresses or violates laws, though the voice of the country requires that he should suffer, yet he will never feel that remorse of conscience that the other will, and that keen, cutting reflection will never rise in his breast that otherwise would, had he done the deed, or committed the offense in full conviction that he was breaking the law of his country, and having previously acknowledged the same to be just. It is not our intention by these remarks, to attempt to place the law of man on a parallel with the law of heaven; because we do not consider that it is formed in the same wisdom and propriety; neither do we consider that it is sufficient in itself to bestow anything on man in comparison with the law of heaven, even should it promise it. The laws of men may guarantee to a people protection in the honorable pursuits of this life, and the temporal happiness arising from a protection against unjust insults and injuries; and when this is said, all is said, that can be in truth, of the power, extent, and influence of the laws of men, exclusive of the law of God. The law of heaven is presented to man, and as such guarantees to all who obey it a reward far beyond any earthly consideration; though it does not promise that the believer in every age should be exempt from the afflictions and troubles arising from different sources in consequence of the acts of wicked men on earth. Still in the midst of all this there is a promise predicated upon the fact that it is the law of heaven, which transcends the law of man, as far as eternal life the temporal; and as the blessings which God is able to give, are greater than those which can be given by man. Then, certainly, if the law of man is binding upon man when acknowledged, how much more must the law of heaven be! And as much as the law of heaven is more perfect than the law of man, so much greater must be the reward if obeyed. The law of man promises safety in temporal life; but the law of God promises that life which is eternal, even an inheritance at God's own right hand, secure from all the powers of the wicked one.
	\item[CDBY 27] 1. Can any officer in any branch of the Church say that his word is law and shall be obeyed? Answer: He can say that his word is law; but does that make it so? Yes, if he has the law of God and delivers it: otherwise it is not.
	\item[CDBY 33] I wish to speak on the duty of lawyers, as they have been spoken of this morning. They were first among the children of Israel to explain the laws of Moses to the common people. I class myself as a lawyer in Israel. My business is to make peace among the people; and when any man who calls himself a lawyer takes a course to break peace instead of making it, he is out of the fine of his duty. A lawyer's duty is to read the law well himself, then tell the people what it is, and let them act upon it, and keep peace; and let them receive pay like any laboring man. It is desirable for justices of the peace, when men call for writs, to inquire into the merits of the case, and tell the parties how to settle it, and thus put down lawsuits. To cure lawing, let us pay attention to our business.
	\end{description}

% -----------------------
\subsection{Law of Christ} % *LAWOFCHRIST *LAWCHRIST
% -----------------------

	See also ``doctrine of Christ,'' as in 2N 31, especially verse 7. Not quite sure of the relationship yet though. Think also of the ``gospel of Jesus Christ,'' which is related here; in a sense you might think narrowly of the ``law of Christ'' as the gospel as defined in a scripture like DC 39:6. Think of ``fulness of the gospel'' in this sense too, either in the narrow or broad sense of law of Christ?
	
	Related to the office of Messiah; in fact, I think that whoever has the office of Messiah is the one of whom there's a universal law, like the law of Christ. Remember that ``Messiah'' and ``Christ'' both mean ``anointed'' in Hebrew and Greek, respectively. It's two different ways of saying the same thing. Very interesting idea.
	
	Think also about ``demands of justice'' here. It wouldn't be just if there were a law (here, of Christ) of some being, which applied so extensively, without that being descending below all things? Cf. Al 34:16. This is related to the power of atonement as well---to have that power is to be a being of whom it can be said, ``there is a law OF that being.''
		Not sure if that last part is exactly right, but it is interesting in 3N 27, for example, where it talks about Christ drawing all men to him (or having the power to do so), it talks about that in connection with his sacrifice.
		
	See also ``rights of mercy,'' ``priesthood,'' ``light of christ,''

I class myself as a lawyer in Israel. My business is to make peace among the people; and when any man who calls himself a lawyer takes a course to break peace instead of making it, he is out of the fine of his duty. A lawyer's duty is to read the law well himself, then tell the people what it is, and let them act upon it, and keep peace; and let them receive pay like any laboring man. It is desirable for justices of the peace, when men call for writs, to inquire into the merits of the case, and tell the parties how to settle it, and thus put down lawsuits. JSP-D4 contains this quote: ``Perhaps the most direct evidence of Rigdon's involvement is Brigham Young's characterization of the lectures in 1860 as ones 'Brother Sidney prepared.' % -----------------------
\subsection{Lecture at the veil} % *LECTUREVEIL *LECTUREATTHEVEIL
% -----------------------

	There are at least three things that could be called the ``lecture at the veil.''
		The first is the set of instructions that we currently receive in the endowment ceremony right before we do the ceremony at the veil.
		The second seems more clearly to be a ``lecture'' and was given only when there were new temple visitors who were receiving their own endowment (MEC 98). This lecture is at MEC 98--101. I haven't read the whole thing yet but it looks like a summary of the entire ceremony.
		The third is the original lecture at the veil, delivered by BY in the St. George Temple in February 1877, and written down by his scribes. Contains some Adam-God materials. According to the records BY reviewed their transcript of his words himself and made corrections. He seems to have revised again later too, and L. John Nuttall noted some of those changes in his journal. And since the real copy of this lecture has never been available---as far as I know it's still in the St. George temple---the only record we have, I think, is Nuttall's journal. See MG 110--113 for a discussion and the entry in the journal.
			For a more extended discussion, see UR part 75 and the notes for part 75 (113--118, 165--176; this latter bit is a lot about the Bunkerville issue with Adam-God).
			From reading some of the stuff in UR, it does seme like the pre-1990 ``lecture at the veil'' (the second one above) is a modification of the original; I'll have to look at this more closely in the future.
			The Adam-God parts appear to have been taken out in early 1900 (as in the first few years of the century).
		
	Other sources that don't offer much more:
		DLDSTW 36--38, 173

% -----------------------
\subsection{Levels principle} % *LEVELS
% -----------------------

	See truth as goodness; golden compass metaphor; universality of the gospel; epistemology of revelation; language; light; accountability; translation; mysteries; will of god; key; judgment;
		See also:
			book of mormon, especially the parts about it being a long revelation;

	The Levels Principle is the idea that everything God reveals to us, and everything he does in relation to our salvation, occurs in a certain context; and if the context were different, God's revelations, instructions, and actions would be different. In other words, God changes the way he works with us according to our standing with respect to various \textit{levels}--biological, cognitive, financial, and so on.

	At first this principle seems almost self-evident--of course God would provide a certain type of help to someone in situation A, while helping someone else different in situation B, where A and B are distinct. But this principle becomes much more powerful when it is extended to \textit{everything} that God does, all His interactions with us, and when we realize that the principle scales to the size of the world and beyond, to all existence. Reality presents God a framework within which to work, and so He does.
	
	We already understand the principle in the way of Al 12:9--11---the ``levels'' in those verses are personal and group righteousness. But the principle becomes much more powerful when we realize that there are other levels \textit{which we can't control}---many levels that influence God's interaction with us, but which are not within our ability to change, and maybe not even within our ability to know about. You get the levels principle when you apply Al 12:9--11 to scales and measures that we don't have any control over.
	
	Another way to think about levels is in conjunction with the idea of the revelations of God ``unfolding'' to our view; from wherever we stand, we have a distorted perspective, can't see all the towel, some parts of the towel are nearer our vision than others, etc.
	
	See DC 130, the verses about laws and blessings, as a special case of levels principle?

	Here are a few other important aspects of this principle:

		\begin{compactitem}
		\item As we are righteous and obedient, we receive more light from God.
		\item We may discover that something we believe to be the incontrovertible truth, or irrefutable doctrine, is not so. I like how Konrad Lorenz puts it: ``Our working hypothesis should read as follows: Everything is a working hypothesis.''
		\item If our understanding of the gospel is always a working hypothesis, we face another problem. We have to decide whether the fact that something in the gospel is a certain way on this earth implies that it will always be that way, even in eternity, or that what we observe on this earth is just an instance of an eternal principle. You might think this, for example:
			\begin{description}
			\item[Reflection Principle] The organization and implementation of the gospel on earth always reflects the organization and implementation of the gospel in eternity. 
			\end{description}
		I personally think that the Reflection Principle stated in this way is much too strong, but if we weaken it (``\textit{sometimes} reflects the organization...''), then we face an epistemic problem: how can we discern between an earthly manifestation of an eternal principle, and a way of doing things which only obtains because it was the best thing that could have happened, given the circumstances?
		I find this problem extremely important and believe that many, many errors in thinking about the gospel are caused by a failure to bring these kinds of questions to the front.
		\item The levels principle also explains scriptures like 2N 26:13 and especially 2N 27:23, where God works (and only works) according to our faith. Part of our faith is a cognitive component, meaning it has a particular content, and so God must act in accordance with that content. These scriptures about God acting in accordance with our faith are instances of the levels principle.
		\item This is wrapped up with mysterianism--there are just things that we do not know right now, or cannot know. This is a fact which must figure in our theorizing. There are things that we cannot perceive right now; there are things that we cannot cognize right now; there are things that are just beyond us right now.
		\item Remember to include the idea of unfolding.
		\item I dislike the name ``levels principle,'' but right now I don't have anything else to say. For the meantime, then, a partial list of levels:
			\begin{compactdesc}
			\item[linguistic]
			\item[conceptual]
			\item[biological]
			\item[financial]
			\item[neurological] This kind of goes with biological and cognitive, but is a little different. Think of Aaron Batista's work on intrinsic manifolds, and things that are more or less difficult to learn. They're more or less difficult because of the neural population activities that are available to us---they kind of determine what is possible for us to do. So see the brain as the limiting factor, or a very great limiting factor, in the levels principle. Something like the brain's available neural populations and activities underlies (or is part of) the levels principle. It's the brain that's holding us back somehow. 
			
			So think of spiritual learning---I mean just done by the spirit, before the union of spirit and body---as re-organizing of spiritual matter, or the re-organizing of whatever things make a spirit cognitive. Maybe it's just a lot easier to do because the reorganizing processes for spiritual matter are very different and easier to accomplish; it's harder with the brain. So when you see something like 2N 9:13, talking about a perfect knowledge, it could be a purification or enhancement of the brain allowing it to acquire and retain knowledge more easily (like the spirit might naturally, without the body).
			\item[cognitive]
			\item[gospel knowledge]
			\item[general cultural background]
			\item[individual cultural background] This level includes prejudices and biases.
			\item[spatial location] Globally and locally---what world do you live on? As in, what planet? It could make a difference, for all we know. But also, what country do you live in? What is the relationship of that country to others? What state, what county, what city, what neighborhood, what house, what family?
			\item[general level of scientific understanding]
			\item[individual level of scientific understanding]
			\end{compactdesc}
		\item The epistemology of revelation, at least in part, determines how the church is organized; the organization of the church is a partially an epistemic organization, or organized in a way as to facilitate an epistemic structure for administering God's word to the people on earth.
		\end{compactitem}
		
	Here are some examples of the principle, from the scriptures and other sources.

		\begin{description}
		\item[1N 1:2] (A ``languge'' here consists of an actual written language and a system of ``learning.'' You see later, where Mormon or Moroni is writing, I think in Ether, that both of these affect what makes it onto the plates. See 2N 31:3, which combined with this scripture is an extremely clear statement of the levels principle.) Yea, I make a record in the language of my father, which consists of the learning of the Jews and the language of the Egyptians.
			\begin{compactitem}
			\item See also 1N 3:19--20, where Nephi speaks about the importance of getting the record from Laban: ``And behold, it is wisdom in God that we should obtain these records, that we may preserve unto our children the language of our fathers; 20 And also that we may preserve unto them the words which have been spoken by the mouth of all the holy prophets, which have been delivered unto them by the Spirit and power of God, since the world began, even down unto this present time.''
			\item And 1N 5:21: ``And we had obtained the records which the Lord had commanded us, and searched them and found that they were desirable; yea, even of great worth unto us, insomuch that we could preserve the commandments of the Lord unto our children.''
			\item 1N 10:15 (see a few verses before this---shows an example of the kind of teaching being done according to the language.) And after this manner of language did my father prophesy and speak unto my brethren, and also many more things which I do not write in this book; for I have written as many of them as were expedient for me in mine other book.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.

And it mattereth not to me that I am particular to give a full account of all the things of my father, for they cannot be written upon these plates, for I desire the room that I may write of the things of God. 4 For the fulness of mine intent is that I may persuade men to come unto the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, and be saved. 5 Wherefore, the things which are pleasing unto the world I do not write, but the things which are pleasing unto God and unto those who are not of the world. 6 Wherefore, I shall give commandment unto my seed, that they shall not occupy these plates with things which are not of worth unto the children of men.
